subject: Next steps: global deep-dive + proposed rotating demo rhythm
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Liu <h.liu@acme-insights.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up + proposed global rotation windows (post-discovery)

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to get a clear read on the two priority streams: (1) embedding search latency at scale for the customer-facing product and (2) a private deployment option for regulated telemetry. Quick recap and suggested next steps below.

Recap (short):
- Pain: current embedding costs & tail latency at 99th percentile during peak queries.
- Constraint: must keep production data in-region for EU customers; APAC team needs a path to private deployment.
- Success metric: 2x cost reduction on embeddings + 50ms improvement at P99 or safe fallback behavior.

Proposed next step: 60-minute technical deep dive (demo + infra Q&A) with engineering and security stakeholders. Because the team spans US / EU / APAC, I propose we adopt a rotating demo cadence so all regions get a friendly local time slot across the next three weeks. Two lightweight options:

Option A — Weekly rotating windows (recommended):
- Week 1 (US friendly): Tue 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET (good for US morning)
- Week 2 (EU friendly): Wed 11:00 BST / 12:00 CET (midday EU)
- Week 3 (APAC friendly): Thu 17:00 IST / 20:00 SGT (late APAC)

Option B — Fixed tri-zone set on alternating days (less rotation, more predictability):
- Monday: US window, Wednesday: EU window, Friday: APAC window (repeat).

Practical asks for the deep dive:
- Can you confirm the core technical attendees we should include (engineering, infra, security)? You mentioned Rajiv and a security lead — please confirm names.
- Is 60 minutes okay or would you prefer 45 minutes?
- Any materials you want upfront (SOC 2 excerpt, example request patterns)? I’ve attached our call notes and a suggested agenda.

Proposed concrete slot candidates (please pick 1–2):
- Tue Jul 20, 2026 — 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET / 18:00 BST
- Wed Jul 21, 2026 — 11:00 BST / 12:00 CET / 06:00 PT
- Thu Jul 22, 2026 — 17:00 IST / 20:30 SGT / 09:00 BST

If you’re comfortable with a rotating approach, we can mark the first deep dive in whichever window works best and then rotate the subsequent calls. I’ll coordinate invitations and include a short demo script tailored to your embedding workload.

Attachments: discovery-notes.pdf (recap), suggested-agenda.docx (inline in notes)

Thanks,

Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Hannah Liu <h.liu@acme-insights.com>

Cc: Rajiv Patel <r.patel@acme-insights.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:47:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up + proposed global rotation windows (post-discovery)

Thanks Olga — great summary. Quick answers below:

- Attendees: please include Rajiv (infra lead, India), me (product), and I’ll invite our security lead — name: Priya Shah (cc’d once she confirms).
- Duration: 45 minutes would be better for our engineers.
- Preference: We prefer Option A (weekly rotation) but would ask that the APAC slot be slightly earlier in IST if possible (17:00 IST is OK but 16:30 IST is preferable for our team).

From the proposed concrete slots, the Thu Jul 22 APAC slot looks promising if you can nudge it to 16:30 IST / 20:00 SGT. Otherwise Wed Jul 21 (11:00 BST) also works for EU folks.

I’m attaching our availability (.ics) — can you confirm whether you need any specific telemetry samples ahead of the demo? Also, if you can share a short SOC 2 excerpt that covers network controls, that’ll speed our security review.

Attachment: acme-availability.ics

Best,
Hannah

Subject: RE: Follow-up + proposed global rotation windows (post-discovery) — internal coordination

Team — Hannah prefers Option A (weekly rotation) and asks APAC slot to be 16:30 IST if we can accommodate. She prefers a 45-minute deep dive and will include Rajiv (infra) and Priya (security) on their side. Action items below:

- Aditya: please prepare a 20–25 minute demo focused on embedding batching/kv-cache behavior and a short section (5–10 min) about cost controls (quantization + batching knobs). Include an example request pattern from the notes.
- Monica: can you pull a SOC 2 excerpt (network controls + data segregation) and a one-page summary we can send to Hannah before the call? She asked specifically for network controls. (Attachment name suggestion: SOC2-excerpt.pdf)
- Marcus: please set up a provisional calendar invite with three slot options so we can let Hannah pick (include our rotating-cadence note in the invite). Use the HubSpot deal link in the invite and mark as "tentative" until Hannah confirms.

Proposed final slot candidates adjusted per Hannah:
1) Wed Jul 21, 2026 — 11:00 BST / 06:00 PT (45 minutes)
2) Thu Jul 22, 2026 — 16:30 IST / 20:00 SGT (45 minutes)
3) Tue Jul 20, 2026 — 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET (45 minutes)

I’ll send the SOC2 excerpt and the demo script to Hannah once ready. Marcus — please hold all three and include Rajiv’s email once he’s in the final list.
